decisions.reason: The ID Vault was publicly announced with a dedicated press release as a groundbreaking feature, and it is central to KOBIL's digital identity direction, so management is committed to it and will justify keeping it.
The identity-bound wallet ties directly into KOBIL's announced super-app and identity strategy, so weak early visibility can be put down to the market still ramping up rather than to failure.
The NFC login authenticator is less central and only mentioned on the site, but it extends the authentication portfolio the firm has invested in, so management will likely keep it for now.
The payment and wallet framework has its own page and supports the firm's platform strategy, which signals strong investment and visible commitment.
The multi-service mobile app platform is the core of KOBIL's announced super-app direction, so dropping it would contradict earlier decisions and public statements.
The application shielding library has its own page and builds on long-standing mobile security investments, so the firm will persist with it.
